additionalProperties.value: Programs hardware AES MMIO at 38c00000. Rejects zero or non-16-byte-multiple length. Handles supplied 16-byte key for key selector 0, selectors 1/2 also accepted, loads IV registers +74..80, programs input/output buffers and starts operation. Register mapping corroborated against local Rockbox s5l87xx.h. Exact meanings of nonzero key selectors not asserted.
Lazily creates mutex, serializes access, calls Crypto_AESProcessBufferHardware, unlocks.

Copies a media-list entry into destination list. Third argument is insertion cursor, checked by MediaList_ValidateInsertionCursor then passed to MediaList_LinkEntryAfterCursor. Normal OTG append callers pass NULL. Nested-entry and duplicate-suppression behavior present; use existing allocator/notifications, not raw node allocation. Play Next feasibility lead; active playback/shuffle synchronization remains unverified.

Decodes setting via 0807bef8, updates uint16 settings+0xb64 if changed, calls 08053794, then TPodMediaPlayer vtable+0xa0 (08171b98) with low byte. Analyst-assigned role; exact input ABI is not fully typed.

2026-09-12 startup investigation: two passes over 21 task descriptors (0x1a4/0x14). First creates tasks through 080f8fc0 -> 080f8f84; second starts them through 080f8fc4 -> IRAM22003e00. Table constructor includes GraphicsManager. UI can run concurrently before startup task reaches its later return checkpoint.

Decodes filename in four-byte groups: output {input[2]^ca,input[0]^a6,input[3]^01,input[1]^4a}; creates path object under caller base path. Call-site literals 08067120..08067134 decode to IC-Info.sidb, .sidd, .sidv, .sidr, .sidl, .rbSyncResp. This constructs path objects; it is not itself full ticket verification.

Context-based decryption wrapper used for game executable (080f9664) and media buffers (080ed030). Calls 0831bf88, which processes 16-byte blocks and reaches hardware AES via 0835e1f4 -> 0802ea90. Requires usable context; success bypass does not replace decryption.

Obfuscated context setup, called during library initialization with iPod_Control/iTunes/ and an 8-byte identifier; game built-in/storage mode 4 may create a separate game-path context with 6-byte identifier. Initializes IC-Info.sidb/sidd/sidv/sidr/sidl/rbSyncResp storage objects. Filename decoding in 0805ecb4. Exact key derivation/device binding unresolved.

Verified insertion semantics from ARM/decompiler: cursor is {parent, predecessor}. NULL cursor appends under list root; predecessor -1 selects tail; predecessor 0 inserts at head; other predecessor inserts AFTER that node. Node +8=next,+0xc=previous,+4=parent. Updates root/ancestor counts and invalidates order caches. Low-level list insertion, NOT by itself a complete player queue operation.

Recovered role from exact preset-name comparisons. Converts a length-prefixed name to IDs 100..121 (Acoustic..Vocal Booster), otherwise 0. Used by settings migration. Analyst-assigned name, not an original symbol.

Game API module lookup: follows linked registry at 08a0fc88 up to 08a1070c, compares 32-byte module names. Registry contains Audio, Metadata, SoundEffect, AsyncFileIO, MemoryAlloc, InputEvents, Settings, OpenGLES, Users, DebugUtil, miscTBD. Located while investigating Phase; no Phase-specific caller confirmed.

Order-mode normalization. Special mode 0x33 used by playback traversal maps to list+0xc8 when list+0x18c bit0 clear, or mode2 when set; zero mode falls back to1. This is why physical linked-list insertion alone does not establish Play Next behavior for all sort/shuffle modes.
Maps settings IDs 100..121 to DSP presets 1..22; other inputs return 0. Verified switch. DSP 0 is bypass; settings ID 107 (Flat) maps to 8. Analyst-assigned name.

Resolves integer handle through game metadata registry at GameMetadata service +0. Corrected erroneous no-return flag; returns object or NULL. Metadata wrappers previously analyzed with truncated bodies must be checked against bounded disassembly.

Called by GameRuntime_LoadExecutableAndResolveImports. Validates game import descriptors, finds named OS modules through GameAPI_FindModuleByName, checks 16-byte interface identity and function count, copies import stubs/table words, returns up to five game entry points. Confirms OS-provided game API. No bypass/firmware changes made.
Builds Manifest.plist and Manifest.plist.p7b paths using table 089cc9f0, invokes manifest reader with signature companion.
Iterates manifest file entries except selected executable, checks file sizes and invokes 082cc5e8 when Verify flag is set. Does not request a decryption context for these resource checks.

Loads manifest and verifies non-executable files, selects platform executable, reads it, optionally loads <executable>.sinf (max 0x4000 bytes) when file DRM flag +0x19 is set. Verify flag +0x18 gates 082cc5e8; executable path requires success and non-null output context. DRM flag then gates in-place FairPlay_DecryptBuffer. The context creation/key derivation inside obfuscated backend remains unresolved; returning success alone does not decrypt bytes.

FW2.0.4 version property0x6402 builds numeric version then platform suffix. Experimental 16-byte inline CFW suffix patch was uploaded 2026-09-12, but user reports CFW did not show. About-screen binding is NOT confirmed; upload success cannot exclude stock reset/fallback. Original bytes retained here. Next experiment directly changes English SettingsMenu_About_String at087f6f3c. See OSOS-ABOUT.md and OSOS-ABOUT-MENU.md.

Algorithm: rejects context handle -1. Selector r2: 0 -> Audio_SetPostEffectsGainQ15(context,*payload); 1 -> 0818c28c(context,payload); 2 -> Audio_SetEQPreset(context,*payload); 3 -> no-op 0818c310. Others return -1. Parameters: r1 context, r2 property selector, r3 payload; r0 unused here. Returns: 0 for recognized selectors, -1 invalid. EQ UI handoff 081a5bdc -> IRAM 2200508c -> 22003700 -> this function, verified against preserved startup bytes.

Primary TPodMediaPlayer vtable +0x128. Appends selection to list wrapper this+0x60 (raw list pointer this+0x64), using supplied browsing context or this+0x9a8. Called by OnTheGo_AddSelection when player flag this+0x93f is set. Existing live-list update path; does not expose destination insertion cursor.

Prepares next track under player lock this+0xa4c. Resolves current index through primary vtable +0x158 and PlaybackList_GetEntryByIndex, calls MediaPlayer_FindNextPlayableEntry(mode=3), allocates 0x24-byte next-track object at this+0x58 if absent, then activates it via 081732e8. Important for Play Next: inserting a list entry may leave this prepared candidate stale. Correct cancellation/refresh path not yet established.

Singleton accessor used by all Audio module wrappers at 082bbb94..082bbfff. Corrected erroneous no-return flag: function does return on initialized path. Existing caller function bodies may still need bounded repair to include instructions beyond previously marked terminal call.

Algorithm: adjusts r0 context to embedded EQ object at +0x18034, then tail-calls EQ_SetDspPreset (08271cf4). Parameters: r0 audio context; r1 DSP preset 0..22. Returns: follows EQ setter. Analyst-assigned name, supported by direct branch and EQ constructor placement.

Algorithm: iterates three effect objects at this+0x2a190/+0x2a194/+0x2a198. Checks vtable+0x0c and processes enabled stages through +0x1c, propagating buffer pointer and frame count. Audio_InitEffectsChain places EQ at index 1 (this+0x18034). Only AFTER all three effects, 0818c3d0..0818c420 multiplies each stereo S16 sample by this+0x2a170 and arithmetic-shifts 15, unless gain >=0x7fff (bypass). Then optional diagnostic WAV output and downstream output-service handoff. Parameters: r0 context, r2 PCM pointer, r3 stereo frame count; remaining output-service ABI not fully typed. Returns: not established. Static conclusion: this gain is post-EQ and cannot prevent clipping already produced by EQ_ProcessBiquadStereoS16. It does not establish absence of gain elsewhere upstream.

Algorithm: stores unsigned gain at this+0x2a170; values >=0x8000 clamp to 0x7fff. Audio_ProcessEffectsAndOutput uses it AFTER all effects, including EQ, as sample*gain >>15, with 0x7fff treated as exact bypass. Parameters: r0 audio context, r1 gain. Returns: void. Property selector 0 reaches this setter via Audio_DispatchPropertyUpdate. This is not an EQ precut.

Algorithm: initializes three effect objects and stores their pointers at context+0x2a190 (context+4, format/rate conversion inferred from 0818c530), +0x2a194 (context+0x18034, verified EQ), +0x2a198 (context+0x180ec, additional effect initialized by 08284af8). Disables each via vtable+8. Sets post-effects gain +0x2a170 to 0x7fff (bypass), default format 44100 Hz/16-bit/stereo. Parameters: r0 context. Returns: context. These are three audio effects; EQ itself contains three biquad stages. Analyst-assigned name.
Within Files (token 7), handles DRM token 3 -> entry+0x19 and Verify token 0x14 -> entry+0x18. Token names in table 083f1910.

Song-list context menu builder. Reached via controller vtable +0x148 from MediaList_HandleShowContextualMenu. Builds 12-byte entries through ContextMenuItems_Append, including HandleStartGenius and HandleAddToOTG; saves highlighted row at this+0xe8 and calls UI_ShowContextMenuItems. Candidate UI hook for Play Next; no firmware patch or device test performed.
Reads .p7b companion and passes manifest bytes, manifest length, signature bytes, signature length to 08052b30. Success iff backend returns zero. Full certificate/trust policy not yet reconstructed.

Verified: preset at this+0xb4, sample rate this+4, enable byte this+8. For nonzero preset and 44100/48000 Hz, uses coefficient banks 088feb54/088fef8c. Preset map 088ff3c4 has 23 rows x 3 signed indices; -1 bypasses a stage. Each 20-byte coefficient record is [b0,b1,b2,a1,a2], signed integers with 24 fractional bits. Three stage states spaced 0x38; coefficients at this+stage*0x38+0x14/18/1c/0c/10. Other rates/preset zero clear enable. Static analysis only.
Clears eight 32-bit delay values for one stage, indexed by r1, stride 0x38. State at this+stage*0x38+0x20..0x3c: x1 L/R, x2 L/R, y1 L/R, y2 L/R. Coefficients are retained.

Stores preset 0..22 at this+0xb4, clamps out-of-range to bypass 0, loads coefficients, invokes vtable+0x10 (reset states in identified EQ vtable). Reached through audio property selector 2 via 0815c830 -> 0818c1b0. Analyst-assigned name.
If sample rate differs, stores this+4, reloads EQ coefficients and invokes vtable+0x10 to reset state. Identified loader supports 44100 and 48000 Hz.
Calls EQ_ResetBiquadState for stages 0, 1, 2.

Verified ARM recurrence: y=b0*x+b1*x1+b2*x2-a1*y1-a2*y2. Signed 32-bit coefficients scaled by 2^24, signed 64-bit SMULL/SMLAL accumulation; input S16 is shifted left 9, accumulated value shifted right 24 into 32-bit state, output shifted right 9 and saturated to S16. Separate left/right history; interleaved stereo input/output, frame count r3, stage index stack arg. High-Q/boost headroom and overflow bounds not validated.

Passes input buffer/frame count to outputs, iterates stages 0..2, skips those with bypass byte this+stage*0x38+0x40 nonzero, processes remaining stages in place with EQ_ProcessBiquadStereoS16. Each stage writes saturated S16 samples.
Initializes EQ vtable, preset 0 and disabled flag. All three stages start bypassed with unity b0=0x01000000, other coefficients zero, and cleared history. Does not itself initialize sample rate.

Handles row clipping/selection and child draw slot70. Shared renderer, not proven main-menu-exclusive. Game launch path: constructs Manifest.plist path, reads manifest, prepares resources, loads executable/resolves OS imports, then invokes game callback at runtime object+0x26c. General game infrastructure; not evidence of Phase-specific format handling.
Returns file entry byte +0x18. Parser 08208ec8 writes this for manifest key Verify (token 0x14).
Returns file entry byte +0x19. Parser 08208ec8 writes this for manifest key DRM (token 3).

Game file protection wrapper: called with FairPlay storage context, file bytes/length and manifest digest buffer; executable call additionally passes .sinf bytes/length and output decryption-context pointer. Resource call supplies no .sinf and no output context. Backend 082e12d8 computes/compares a 20-byte digest and can call 082de3c8 to construct context. Exact algorithm, authorization checks and key derivation remain unresolved; do not label as a simple authorization predicate.

2026-09-12: post-final return beep witness uploaded; user observed Apple logo and normal OS without beep/halt. Does NOT prove crash, reset, or that this site executed. Static final callee08081e60 has return paths but dispatches work and synchronization; tasks already started by0805d558. Late IRAM reporter lifetime not proven. Hook bytes/file mapping checked offline.

English SettingsMenu_About_String (ID 0x0dad0b44). Original About plus NUL and padding; full type2 OSOS file offset 0x802614. English record at file 0x41bdd0 = {ID,0x3df614,6}, resource base file0x423000. Separate menu marker candidate replaces five characters with CFW!! without changing length or code. See OSOS-ABOUT-MENU.md. Reference bytes here remain original; device result pending.

Returns heap base from literal 0804b44c (stock 08b32b58) and size = SysInfo RAM base + RAM size - heap base. Caller 0806be98 supplies this region to the main memory-pool initializer. The separate C-runtime heap base literal is 0807bfac. The CFW heap reservation advances both bases past its payload; stack-top literals remain at the original BSS end.
Gets the platform heap region, stores its base/size at manager offsets +0xd8/+0xdc, then calls 080cc0bc to initialize the memory pool.

Allocates a 24-byte message, stores the two tone parameters at +0x10/+0x14, and posts event 5 to task/queue 2 via 0802d058. Used by alarm and alert sequences, including (540,200), (676,200). Exact timing/pitch units have not been independently measured.

Handles ShowSetting_About: selects GotoThreeCard_About or GotoFourCard_About from the accessory query and dispatches the UI action. Called at 0821c960. Original handler and its private literals occupy 0821cf04..0821cf8c.
Looks up a resource by type and ID, returning its data pointer and writing its byte length. For ROM-backed banks (kind 2), checks the override map at +0x18 before falling back to ResourceIndex_Find.
Copies or replaces a resource identified by type and ID. Arguments: bank, type, ID, data pointer, byte length. ROM-backed banks store the copy in their initialized override map.
Allocates the resource override map and stores it at bank+0x18. Called at 081c7410 before UI resource providers are constructed; this call is a candidate CFW resource-registration hook.
Finds a resource type and ID in a version-3 ROM resource index. Returns data-base plus the stored resource offset and writes its byte length. Type and sparse-ID lookups use binary search.
Returns the resource ID associated with a C++ string in the global name-to-ID map. Calls the map indexing operation, which can insert a default entry for an unknown name.
Dispatches Settings action names such as ShowSetting_About and ShowSetting_Legal. A third argument of 0xdeadbeef suppresses execution. Menu navigation also uses serialized CEVT navigator actions.
Builds the UI resource-provider chain. Gets the default resource bank, initializes its override map at call site 081c7410, then constructs and registers providers.

Creates the provider and sets MainMenu_List_Debug (0x0dad01a1) visibility to false. The mov r1,#0 at 0812ad24 supplies the visibility argument; changing it to 1 exposes the existing Extras > Debug entry.
Looks up the ITEM record by item ID, updates its visibility byte at +0x64, and sends LitE/None notifications. Menu-list rebuilding omits records whose visibility byte is zero.
Rebuilds menu-item mappings and provider subscriptions. ITEM records with byte +0x64 equal to zero are omitted from the visible-index vector and visible count.
Waits for LCD_STATUS bit 1, delays, and selects the panel command interface. Panel types 0/1 use 8-bit commands; types 2/3 use 16-bit commands. Returns the previous LCD_CON value.
Waits for LCD_STATUS bit 1, delays, then writes LCD_CON at 0x38300000.
Sets the 8-bit-command panel window with commands 0x2a and 0x2b, issues memory-write command 0x2c, and restores the previous interface configuration.
Sets the 16-bit-command panel window using registers 0x210-0x213, cursor registers 0x200/0x201, and GRAM-write command 0x202. Restores the previous interface configuration.
